import pandas as pd

# File paths for source CSVs
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_52/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_52/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_52/training_2.csv"

# Read source CSVs with index_col=0 to ignore the first index column as per instructions
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)

# All source tables have the same schema and match the target schema column names exactly.
# Operation: UNION all three sources (concatenate)
df_union = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2], ignore_index=True)

# Enforce target schema and types:
# Target schema: ['username': float, 'date': string, 'retweets': integer, 'favorites': integer,
# 'text': string, 'geo': string, 'mentions': string, 'hashtags': string, 'id': float, 'permalink': string]

# Convert columns to target types:
# username: float (source is NaN in examples, so convert to float)
df_union['username'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['username'], errors='coerce')

# date: string (ensure string)
df_union['date'] = df_union['date'].astype(str)

# retweets: integer
df_union['retweets'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['retweets'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# favorites: integer
df_union['favorites'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['favorites'], errors='coerce').fillna(0).astype(int)

# text: string
df_union['text'] = df_union['text'].astype(str)

# geo: string, keep NaN as is (will be saved as empty string or NaN)
df_union['geo'] = df_union['geo'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# mentions: string, keep NaN as is
df_union['mentions'] = df_union['mentions'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# hashtags: string, keep NaN as is
df_union['hashtags'] = df_union['hashtags'].astype(str).replace('nan', pd.NA)

# id: float (some ids are large integers or floats)
df_union['id'] = pd.to_numeric(df_union['id'], errors='coerce')

# permalink: string
df_union['permalink'] = df_union['permalink'].astype(str)

# Save the final dataframe to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_52/target_multisource.csv"
df_union.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source CSV files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_52/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_52/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_52/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2_52_0 and Source2_52_1 on 'id'
df01 = pd.merge(df0, df1, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('_0', '_1'))

# Join the above result with Source2_52_2 on 'id'
df012 = pd.merge(df01, df2, on='id', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_2'))

# Now aggregate to get one row per id, taking max for each column (max on strings picks lex max, but here it is used to pick non-null or consistent value)
# Columns to aggregate: username, date, retweets, favorites, text, geo, mentions, hashtags, permalink
# Group by 'id' only (id is float in target, so keep as is)
agg_dict = {
    'username_0': 'max',
    'username_1': 'max',
    'username': 'max',
    'date_0': 'max',
    'date_1': 'max',
    'date': 'max',
    'retweets_0': 'max',
    'retweets_1': 'max',
    'retweets': 'max',
    'favorites_0': 'max',
    'favorites_1': 'max',
    'favorites': 'max',
    'text_0': 'max',
    'text_1': 'max',
    'text': 'max',
    'geo_0': 'max',
    'geo_1': 'max',
    'geo': 'max',
    'mentions_0': 'max',
    'mentions_1': 'max',
    'mentions': 'max',
    'hashtags_0': 'max',
    'hashtags_1': 'max',
    'hashtags': 'max',
    'permalink_0': 'max',
    'permalink_1': 'max',
    'permalink': 'max'
}

# Because columns are duplicated with suffixes, we need to pick one column per attribute from the joined tables.
# We will pick the max across all columns for each attribute.

# To simplify, create a DataFrame with columns for each attribute by taking max across the three source columns:
df_agg = pd.DataFrame()
df_agg['id'] = df012['id']

# For each attribute, take max across the three columns (some columns may be missing if suffixes not present)
def max_across_cols(df, cols):
    return df[cols].max(axis=1)

df_agg['username'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['username_0', 'username_1', 'username'])
df_agg['date'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['date_0', 'date_1', 'date'])
df_agg['retweets'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['retweets_0', 'retweets_1', 'retweets'])
df_agg['favorites'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['favorites_0', 'favorites_1', 'favorites'])
df_agg['text'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['text_0', 'text_1', 'text'])
df_agg['geo'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['geo_0', 'geo_1', 'geo'])
df_agg['mentions'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['mentions_0', 'mentions_1', 'mentions'])
df_agg['hashtags'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['hashtags_0', 'hashtags_1', 'hashtags'])
df_agg['permalink'] = max_across_cols(df012, ['permalink_0', 'permalink_1', 'permalink'])

# Reorder columns to match target schema
df_agg = df_agg[['username', 'date', 'retweets', 'favorites', 'text', 'geo', 'mentions', 'hashtags', 'id', 'permalink']]

# Convert columns to target types
df_agg['username'] = df_agg['username'].astype(float)
df_agg['date'] = df_agg['date'].astype(str)
df_agg['retweets'] = df_agg['retweets'].astype(int)
df_agg['favorites'] = df_agg['favorites'].astype(int)
df_agg['text'] = df_agg['text'].astype(str)
df_agg['geo'] = df_agg['geo'].astype(str)
df_agg['mentions'] = df_agg['mentions'].astype(str)
df_agg['hashtags'] = df_agg['hashtags'].astype(str)
df_agg['id'] = df_agg['id'].astype(float)
df_agg['permalink'] = df_agg['permalink'].astype(str)

# Write to output CSV
